sample.source: Indeed job search API through the connected job-search tool (P02 to P12); public company job boards on Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby read through their own APIs (P13 to P21); Indeed read in a logged-in browser, covering the fifteen candidates the rate limit had blocked plus two enterprise-targeted searches (P22 to P33); and one posting supplied as text (P01)
searches: AI Platform Engineer: remote, Chicago IL, New York NY, San Francisco CA, Seattle WA, Austin TX, Boston MA, Atlanta GA, Dallas TX; remote contract
Claude Code Copilot developer productivity engineer: remote

Web searches restricted to job-boards.greenhouse.io, boards.greenhouse.io, jobs.lever.co and jobs.ashbyhq.com: "AI Platform Engineer" job; AI coding agents developer productivity Claude Code Cursor platform team; agent platform or agent infrastructure engineer, United States; AI enablement or AI developer productivity engineer; LLM platform, GenAI platform or AI infrastructure engineer, remote US; AI platform, AI tooling or AI productivity engineer, United States
Live board scans, by a script that read each board's public API: six company boards on Greenhouse and two on Ashby
Indeed in the browser, enterprise-targeted: "Gen AI Evaluation" MCP engineer; "GitHub Copilot" enablement engineer (United States)
sample.inclusion: The role's core work is building or running shared AI or agent infrastructure, tooling, guardrails or platforms that other teams, products or agents use. A title alone does not qualify.
sample.exclusion: Forward-deployed and solutions or sales roles, AI trainer and data annotation gigs, general software roles whose AI content is incidental, management and delivery-director roles.
sample.limits: United States only, search terms chosen by the author, one day; Indeed results are relevance-ranked. Staffing firms sometimes repost a client's description. This is a sample, not a survey. The Indeed tool rate-limited the session after 12 postings, so the rest came from company job boards on Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby. Those systems are used mostly by technology companies, which tilts P13 to P21 toward tech employers and away from banks, insurers and government, whose postings usually sit elsewhere. Job-board postings were read as raw text from each board's API, by a script kept with the research rather than in this repository, not through a summarizer. The two enterprise-targeted browser searches were not neutral either: they looked for evaluation, MCP and Copilot-enablement work at employers outside tech. Indeed pages in the browser carried personalization for the logged-in account; only posting text was recorded.
sample.anonymized: Employers are described rather than named, and posting links are withheld (url is null). The codes are as recorded on 2026-09-22.

codebook.type: Primary kind of job: infrastructure (running, serving or training AI at scale), enablement (shared AI capabilities, standards and governance for many internal teams), product-agents (agents or LLM features inside a customer-facing product), coding-agents (coding agents and AI developer tooling in engineering workflows), applied (a domain-specific AI system). alsoType records a clear second kind.
codebook.agents: Builds, runs or governs AI agents (a model calling tools in a loop) or agentic workflows.
codebook.codingAgents: Names or clearly describes AI coding agents or assistants as something the role builds for, operates or requires.
codebook.retrieval: Retrieval-augmented generation, vector databases, embeddings or document-processing pipelines.
codebook.evaluation: Evaluating model or AI output: golden sets, eval harnesses, model judges, quality gates, evaluation pipelines.
codebook.guardrails: Guardrails, governance, policy, permission scoping for AI, or architectural constraints on AI output.
codebook.aiObservability: Monitoring, logging, tracing or metrics for AI or ML systems.
codebook.costControl: Token cost, spend limits, cost attribution, or compute cost optimization for AI.
codebook.humanApproval: Human review queues, approvals, or human-in-the-loop for AI actions.
codebook.security: Security or compliance named as a responsibility or requirement.
codebook.servingOrTraining: Model serving or inference infrastructure, training, fine-tuning or GPU capacity, as required or preferred.
codebook.languages: Named as required or preferred. typescriptOrJavascript includes Node.js and React.
